'''William Lester Self Andrews''' is an American [[chemist]] who makes contributions to the ongoing development of [[quantum chemistry]] of metallic complexes. He is the Professor Emeritus of Chemistry at the [[University of Virginia]]. He won the [[Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy]] in 2010 for "[[vibrational spectroscopy]] in [[cryogenics|cryogenic matrices]] that combined with quantum calculations, has led to the identification and characterization of many molecules, ions, and complexes across the [[periodic table]]".<ref name=aps>{{citation |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Andrews&first_nm=Lester&year=2010 |title=2010 Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy & Dynamics Recipient |publisher=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref>

He was born in [[Lincolnton, North Carolina]].  His first degree was in [[chemical engineering]] at [[Mississippi State University]] in 1963 and his doctorate was in [[physical chemistry]] at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]] in 1966.<ref name=aps/>

[[File:Mercury-tetrafluoride-3D-balls.png|thumb|left|[[Mercury tetrafluoride]]'s structure was studied in the 2007 paper ''Mercury is a Transition Metal: The First Experimental Evidence for HgF<sub>4</sub>'' which Professor Andrews co-authored.<ref>{{citation |author1=X. Wang |author2=L. Andrews |author3=S. Riedel |author4=M. Kaupp |title=Mercury is a Transition Metal: The First Experimental Evidence for HgF<sub>4</sub> |journal= Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. |date=2007 |volume=46 |number=46 |pages=8371–8375 |doi=10.1002/anie.200703710 |pmid=17899620}}</ref>]]
